what: A three panel is laid over one photo panel, once the panel touches the top edge of the screen, it advances to the next photo every 3s starting 2s later — the noise pattern is rotated and pushed toward −45° for the previous photo and 135° for the next while blending (strength 1), rippling as if reflected in water for 1.5s power2.out and then sharpening. With no photo, a placeholder panel drawn in the skin color is blended in. Shaders are precompiled at setup

options.wait: Time to first page turn (sec), default 2
options.at: With enter, it stands at the 15% line from the bottom of the screen — by default, when the head of the panel (or the ancestor chosen by scope) touches the top of the screen
options.scope: Ancestor css to watch for the head (‹section›) — if none, the block itself
options.[data-fx-part=src]: (optional) photo — img src or data-src. Hidden and loaded onto the panel

note: The original builds a separate WebGL panel for each panel (five panels = …five contexts). With many panels you hit the browser context limit (16), so keep it under ten per screen. The original displacement image (disp1.jpg) is not used, it was redrawn with sin noise
